Observation: Publicly available 1024 x 584 JPEG claiming to show a shark on a flooded Houston freeway during Hurricane Harvey. The file was preserved for forensic analysis.
Forensically reported “No Metadata Found.” This exact downloaded copy contains no usable EXIF metadata for date, location, camera, or editing history.

JPEG analysis found no JPEG comment and reported a standard JPEG table quality of 85. The structure was a normal baseline JPEG, which identifies encoding characteristics but does not prove authenticity.
ELA output was mostly dark and showed no decisive localized anomaly at the tested settings. The result is inconclusive and cannot independently authenticate the image.
The photographer’s portfolio shows the shark beside a yellow kayak off South Africa. This is the source scene from which the shark was taken; it is unrelated to Hurricane Harvey.
PolitiFact rated the Harvey shark image “Pants on Fire.” It reported that the composite had circulated since at least 2011 and traced the shark photograph to a 2005 Africa Geographic feature.
Africa Check traced the shark photograph to the September 2005 issue of Africa Geographic and concluded that the highway image was photoshopped.

National Geographic identified Thomas P. Peschak as the photographer, placed the original shark photograph in South Africa, and documented its later reuse in fake disaster images, including Hurricane Harvey posts.
